title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. K is a field of finite type over Q. U_K is a smooth curve over K, presumably anabelian, with geometric fundamental group π. Write E_K = Gal(K̄/K) and E_{U_K} = π_1(U_K). These sit in the fundamental exact sequence 1 → π → E_{U_K} → E_K → 1. The transcriber's Σ and E are both Grothendieck's script ℰ.

A K-rational point ξ of U_K gives a section φ = ξ_*: E_K → E_{U_K}. This is the 'section of the first kind' (première espèce), numbered (29).

The page then varies the base field in two ways.

(i) Composing φ with partial sections of E_K over other groups gives sections of E_{U_K} over those groups. For instance, take a section of E_K → Γ_Q defined over an open subgroup Γ' ⊂ Γ_Q. Such sections exist, e.g. from a rational point of a model of K over a number field. This yields a section of E_{U_K} over Γ', hence a genuine action of Γ' on π by conjugation, not merely an outer action. The same holds for any subfield K' ⊂ K, viewing E_K as lying over E_{K'}. So (29) produces a whole family of sections, one for each sub-situation, defined up to π-conjugacy.

(ii) Grothendieck wants a global view of this family. He wants to compare it with a second family obtained by specialisation. Choose a model S of K and a model X → S of U_K. A point s ∈ S has residue field k(s) = 𝒪_s/𝔪_s. The section given by (29) on the fibre X_s gives a section of E_{X_s} → E_{k(s)}, hence a true action of E_{k(s)} on π. Here the k(s) are not subfields of K but residue fields of local rings, so the two families are not directly comparable.

The sentence breaking off at the bottom continues on the next page. If S has finite relative dimension over a base field k, closed points have residue fields finite over k. Each s then defines a conjugacy class of decomposition subgroups in π_1 of S (or of the relevant generic-point groups). Through these, sections over E_{k(s)} can be compared with the given section over E_K. Grothendieck then claims that the specialised partial section is again of the first kind, namely the one defined by the specialised point f(s).

Purpose: understand how the section conjecture over finitely generated fields interacts with subfields and with specialisation to residue fields. This is the 'functoriality in the base' of sections, a preliminary to reducing questions over f.g. fields to number fields or finite extensions of a base field.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page; it is programmatic.

Gap: for the comparison with residue fields k(s), one needs that the point ξ extends over a neighbourhood of s (good model, ξ ∈ X(S) locally). One also needs that the specialisation of the section via decomposition groups is well-defined up to conjugacy. This only gets sketched on the next page, where the choice of a 'regular complete model' is suggested in the margin.
Sections of E_K over open subgroups of Γ_Q exist only under hypotheses (e.g. K has a model with a rational point over a number field). This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Section of π_1(U_K) → Gal_K attached to a rational point (section of the first kind / geometric section)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Restricting or composing a section with partial sections of E_K over subfields / open subgroups of Γ_Q, giving genuine (not outer) Galois actions on π
ideas.modern_name: Base change / functoriality of sections; lifting outer Galois representations to true actions via sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in anabelian geometry (cf. Stix's monograph on sections)

ideas.what: Comparing sections over K with sections over residue fields k(s) of a model S, via decomposition groups of points of S; the specialised section of a geometric section is the geometric section of the specialised point
ideas.modern_name: Specialisation of sections / reduction of the section conjecture for finitely generated fields to number fields or finite fields
ideas.usually_credited_to: Developed later in the section-conjecture literature (e.g. Stix's work on sections and on specialisation; exact attributions unsure)
ideas.where_published: The f.g.-field section conjecture is stated in the Faltings letter; the specialisation mechanism is not, to my knowledge, spelled out there

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes a systematic 'vue d'ensemble' of the family of sections obtained from one geometric section by varying the base. That family includes subfields K' ⊂ K on one side and residue fields k(s) of a model on the other. He wants to treat these two kinds of 'base change' (subfield vs. specialisation via decomposition groups) uniformly. Such a unified framework, where both kinds of base change are compatible, is not something I know as a standard object.
missed.quote: J'ai envie d'avoir une vue d'ensemble sur cette famille de sections, et de la mettre en relation avec la famille de sections des E_{X_s} sur les E_{K(s)}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Specialisation of sections along decomposition groups is an active tool for reducing the section conjecture over f.g. fields to number fields. A uniform treatment might clarify how far such reductions extend to non-geometric sections. The idea itself is now largely known, so novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programmatic page on the functoriality and specialisation of Galois sections attached to rational points. It is historically interesting as an early (c. 1981) formulation of the specialisation-of-sections idea that later became standard in the section-conjecture literature. It contains no finished result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The symbols transcribed as Σ (previous page) and E are Grothendieck's script ℰ: ℰ_{U_K}, ℰ_K, ℰ_{K'}, ℰ_{X_s}, ℰ_{k(s)}.
'Q_s/m_s' should read '𝒪_s/𝔪_s' (residue fields of local rings).
'(pas seulement ext[?])' is very likely 'pas seulement extérieures', i.e. genuine actions rather than outer actions.
'K(s)' is better read as 'k(s)' (residue field at s), consistent with the next page.
The interlinear insertion above '(ou le conjugué...)' seems to be 'de M des sous-groupes ouvertes Γ' de ...'; it is barely legible.
In 'si on suppose S de dim relative finie sur', the word 'finie' appears struck through, with 'relative' added above.
